article.articleHeadline: Väkivalta hidastaa ebolan torjuntaa Kongossa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Violence slows Ebola containment in Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed 12,000, with violence slowing containment. The health ministry states clashes between rebels and government forces are delaying evacuation of the sick in eastern Congo. The current outbreak is the fastest on record for the disease. Healthcare workers cannot reach villages with many infections and exposed contacts, hindering timely care and disease surveillance. The World Health Organization notes that those infected are unable to access care at clinics, complicating the response to this rapidly spreading outbreak. This report underscores the challenge of coordinating a response while combat operations continue.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴにおける暴力がエボラ対策を遅らせる
triage.triage_reason: エボラ感染者が12,000人を超え、過去最速の拡大ペースであることに加え、紛争により封じ込め活動が妨げられており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 紛争により医療従事者が患者にアクセスできず、サーベイランスと治療が困難な状況。過去最速の感染拡大との記載あり、重大なリスク増大の兆候。

article.articleHeadline: कबूतर की बीट से लेकर गाजरघास तक, इस मौसम में इनसे होने वाली बीमारियां हो सकती हैं खतरनाक
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: From pigeon droppings to crabgrass, the diseases caused by them this season could be dangerous.
article.articleSummary: Pigeon droppings and feathers in Indian urban and rural settings harbor over 20 pathogenic bacteria and fungi, potentially linked to more than 60 diseases, raising respiratory and skin risk as pigeon populations grow in cities. Dry droppings disperse dust carrying spores and antigens; feather-derived matter also disseminates allergens. In November–December, dry air and reduced ventilation indoors intensify respiratory infections, particularly among children, the elderly, asthmatics, and immunocompromised individuals. Separately, Parthenium hysterophorus, or Congress grass/Parthenium (carrot grass), is an invasive weed along roadsides, vacant plots, and fields. It contains sesquiterpene lactones (parthenin) and can irritate crops and be toxic to livestock; continuous exposure among farmers and outdoor workers poses further health risks via pollen and contact. Preventive guidance emphasizes cleanliness, reducing pigeon feeding, weed control, and consulting health professionals for persistent symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ハトの糞からガジャルガス（草）まで、この季節に注意すべき危険な病気
triage.triage_reason: 特定の感染症アウトブレイクではなく、一般的な健康啓発記事であり、異常性や公衆衛生上の緊急性は認められない。
triage.notes: この記事は季節性の一般的健康リスク（ハトの糞やアレルギー性雑草）に関する啓発情報であり、特定の感染症アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報告するものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Gần 800.000 người sẽ được tiếp cận hệ thống cảnh báo sớm sốt xuất huyết
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nearly 800,000 people will have access to an early warning system for dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Ho Chi Minh City is targeted by two climate-related health projects led by Save the Children International in collaboration with the city CDC and social welfare centers. From 2025–2028, six localities (Hiệp Bình ward; An Hội Tây ward; Hiệp Phước commune; Hưng Long commune; Củ Chi commune; Tân Vĩnh Lộc commune) will receive a data-driven dengue early warning system, integrated with prevention, surveillance, and financial protection to improve access to health services for children and families in hardship. The program aims to reach about 790,000 residents with early warning and preventive measures, and to expand financial protection for roughly 50,000 people (including insurance access) and health coverage for about 4,000 vulnerable individuals. In 2026 (week 46), Ho Chi Minh City reported 2,428 dengue cases (up 25.7% from 4-week average), cumulative 49,232; high-incidence areas include Con Dao Special Zone, Ngai Giao, Minh Thanh. MoH involvement anticipated for scale-up.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市、デング熱早期警戒システムで約80万人がアクセス可能に
triage.triage_reason: デング熱症例数の増加（週46時点で前週比25.7%増、累計49,232件）が報告されているが、記事の主旨は気候変動対応型の早期警戒システム導入プログラムの紹介であり、緊急のアウトブレイク対応ではないため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はホーチミン市における国際NGO（Save the Children）とCDCが連携した気候変動対応型デング熱早期警戒・予防プログラムの発表が主旨。デング熱症例の増加傾向（2026年週46時点）は報告されているが、季節性流行の範囲内か否かは記事からは判断できず、今後の症例動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Число заболевших лихорадкой Эбола в ДР Конго превысило 12 тысяч
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola fever cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has exceeded 12,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has risen to 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths since the outbreak began in April 2026, per the DRC’s National Institute for Public Health (INSP). In the last 24 hours, 66 new cases, 37 deaths, and 25 recoveries were reported. UN peacekeepers evacuated medical personnel from Ituri province in the east amid ongoing fighting. There is no licensed vaccine or treatment for the new Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain currently circulating. The World Health Organization says the outbreak is not out of control. The INSP report underscores continued transmission and the public health challenges posed by conflict-affected health delivery in the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ熱感染者数が1万2000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が1万2000例・死者5900例超に拡大し、紛争地域での医療崩壊や新規株(Bundibugyo ebolavirus)に対するワクチン・治療薬の不在など、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するためPICKUPと判定。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療薬が存在しない新規Bundibugyo株の流行、紛争により医療従事者が避難するなど対応能力の低下が懸念される。WHOは『制御不能ではない』としているが、死亡率が高く(約49%)継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Justiça do Quênia suspende obras de centro contra ebola apoiado pelos EUA
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya's judiciary suspends construction of an Ebola treatment center backed by the U.S.
article.articleSummary: Kenya's Supreme Court suspended a 50-bed Ebola quarantine center at Laikipia Air Base near Nanyuki, central Kenya, funded by the United States, after ruling constitutional violations in approving the project and in failing to disclose terms of the U.S. agreement. The court ordered a halt to further construction until conditions were met, including public disclosure of agreement details. The facility, meant to isolate people exposed to Ebola, including Americans, sparked protests. Seven American humanitarian workers quarantined in July in Congo were among those affected. Justice Patricia Nyaundi urged transparency and public consultation. Health Minister Aden Duale was found in contempt for not halting work per prior orders; he said he had ordered suspension. Kenya has reported its first imported Bundibugyo ebolavirus case from Congo via Uganda; by mid-November, two deaths and seven recoveries; no new cases since Oct 19; a 42-day end-date countdown began Nov 11.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア司法当局、米国支援のエボラ治療センター建設を停止
triage.triage_reason: DRC由来のエボラ(Bundibugyo株)がケニアへ輸入され死亡例も発生しており、国際的拡大と社会的・政治的関心（抗議活動、司法介入、大臣の職務停止問題）が顕著なため。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアにおける輸入エボラ症例と治療施設建設を巡る司法・政治的対立だが、感染源はDRCのBundibugyoエボラウイルスアウトブレイクであるため、DRCを発生地域として含めた。ケニア・ウガンダ・米国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 驻马拉维使馆提醒在马拉维中国公民和计划来马人员关注马涉埃博拉疫情预防措施
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chinese Embassy in Malawi reminds Chinese citizens in Malawi and those planning to travel to Malawi to pay attention to the Malawi Ebola outbreak prevention measures.
article.articleSummary: Malawi’s Ebola outbreak continues with rising confirmed cases and is designated a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, signaling cross-border transmission risk. Malawi’s Ministry of Health issued travel-monitoring and prevention measures, effective immediately. The Chinese Embassy in Malawi urges Chinese citizens and travelers to observe: all entrants must complete the Traveller Health Declaration Form on arrival or beforehand; travelers from or via the Democratic Republic of Congo must self-isolate for 21 days with daily professional health monitoring; travelers from or via Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria must undergo 21 days of daily health monitoring; airports and land borders will conduct temperature checks and health screening; those with Ebola- or other infectious-disease symptoms should report to health workers or nearby medical facilities and call the Malawi public health hotline 929. All travelers, transport operators and border personnel must follow infection-prevention measures and cooperate with border officials; if contamination occurs, disinfection at entry is required. Contacts: Emergency Medical Rescue 998; embassy consular protection +265-888998037; WhatsApp +265-888998010; mlw_lingbao on WeChat; 24/7 consular emergency: +86-10-12308 or +86-10-65612308.

triage.headline_ja: 駐マラウイ中国大使館、マラウイのエボラ出血熱流行に関する予防措置について在マラウイ中国公民および渡航予定者に注意喚起
triage.triage_reason: マラウイでのエボラ出血熱流行がPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）に指定されたとされ、越境感染リスクや渡航制限措置が明記されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はマラウイでのエボラ流行であり、マラウイは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空。DRC・ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアは渡航経由地としての言及であり、発生国としての記載ではないため除外。PHEIC指定の真偽・出典は本文からは確認できず、続報での検証が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ngăn chặn nguy cơ bệnh dại ở Cà Mau
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Preventing the Rabies Risk in Cà Mau
article.articleSummary: Rabies risk in Ca Mau Province, Vietnam. After seven residents in the U Minh and Nguyen Phich communes were attacked by a dog suspected of rabies, Ca Mau provincial authorities rapidly implemented a coordinated response to prevent disease spread. Measures included containment in affected areas, active contact tracing, and ring vaccination around the exposure sites. The incident underscores a potential transmission risk from a dog with suspected rabies and prompts proactive public health actions to protect residents and animals nearby. No laboratory confirmation details are provided in the report, and there is no mention of additional cases beyond the seven initial injuries. The response focuses on short-term containment and vaccination to avert an outbreak, reporting date 2026-11-26, in Ca Mau Province, Vietnam (U Minh and Nguyen Phich communes).

triage.headline_ja: カマウ省で狂犬病リスクを防止
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病疑いの犬による咬傷事例が発生し地域当局が対応を実施しているが、検査確定情報がなく、散発的な動物咬傷事案として国際的な公衆衛生上の深刻性は低いため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 狂犬病疑いの犬による咬傷事例で、地方当局が封じ込め・接触者追跡・リングワクチン接種を実施。検査確定情報なし、追加症例の報告もないため現時点ではローカルな動物由来健康リスク事案と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Temporal molecular features of hepatic injury in mice infected with Echinococcus multilocularis revealed by DIA-based quantitative proteomics
article.articleSummary: Alveolar echinococcosis (AE) caused by Echinococcus multilocularis induces progressive hepatic injury in a mouse model. In C57BL/6 mice, livers were collected at 1, 3 and 6 months post-infection. Histology showed early mild hepatocellular edema, middle-stage inflammatory cell–encapsulated metacestode vesicles, and late-stage extensive fibrotic remodeling. DIA-based quantitative proteomics identified 8537 proteins, with 1140 differentially expressed and 75 persistently altered across stages. Early infection featured cytochrome P450–mediated metabolic stress and mitochondrial dysfunction; the middle stage marked a transition with Ahr/JAK-STAT signaling linked to immune imbalance and incipient fibrogenesis; the late stage corresponded to sustained inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Core proteins Ahr, Thy1, Rtn4 and Prlr displayed stage-specific patterns, with Thy1 increasing throughout and Ahr/Rtn4/Prlr peaking around month 3. The authors propose a triphasic injury model and provide a hepatic proteomic atlas to monitor progression and identify therapeutic targets, based in Xinjiang, China.

triage.headline_ja: DIA定量プロテオミクスにより明らかになった多包条虫感染マウスの肝障害の経時的分子特徴
triage.triage_reason: 本研究はマウスモデルを用いた基礎研究であり、実際のヒトまたは動物の感染アウトブレイクを報告するものではないため、公衆衛生上のシグナルには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti'nde Ebola salgını büyüyor: Can kaybı 6 bine yaklaştı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak is growing in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: death toll nears 6,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 12,000 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths as of 20 November, eight of 26 provinces affected, with Ituri in the northeast the outbreak’s origin since May. Caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain. Delayed detection and strained health systems, compounded by intensified fighting between armed groups and security forces, hinder containment and drive civilian displacement and health-worker risk. UN reports escalating clashes in Ituri; about 12 people (including two WHO staff) were evacuated from Akwe to Bunia after days of heavy fighting, and a humanitarian team sheltered at a UN base before reaching Bunia. Since May, cases have appeared in Uganda, France, Kenya, and Nigeria; Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 case evacuated to Switzerland) saw no new cases by mid-November, with a 42-day monitoring period to declare end. WHO indicates the outbreak remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern as of 18 November.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の流行が拡大：死者数が6000人に迫る
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言しており、死者数約6000人、複数国への拡大、ワクチン未承認の株、武力紛争による対応困難が重なりIHR基準を複数満たすため。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases exceed 12,000 in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo exceed 12,000, and authorities, having faced multiple persistent Ebola outbreaks, are intensifying rigorous epidemiological surveillance and strengthening measures to curb the spread of the virus. Ebola remains a severe viral disease with potential for rapid clinical deterioration and high mortality rates during some outbreaks. Separately, Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient and is awaiting an outbreak-free declaration, signaling regional progress toward containment. As of 26 November 2026, DR Congo continues to implement heightened ongoing surveillance and enhanced ongoing public health measures to limit further spread within its borders.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱症例が12,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ症例が12,000人を超え、公衆衛生上深刻な影響があり、ヒト-ヒト感染リスクと国際的拡大の懸念から、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ケニアは最後の患者が退院し発生終息宣言待ちの段階であり、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCが主な発生地域として継続的なサーベイランスと対策強化が行われている。

article.articleHeadline: Tovább terjed az ebolajárvány a Kongói Demokratikus Köztársaságban
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 12,021 confirmed Ebola infections and 5,904 deaths from the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant. The outbreak began in May in Ituri province, in the north‑east, and has spread to eight of the country’s 26 provinces. There is no approved antiviral treatment or vaccine for this variant. A major containment challenge is that only about 15% of new cases are linked to contacts identified by health authorities, suggesting many transmission chains remain undetected. This outbreak is the second-largest and deadliest Ebola crisis on record, exceeded only by the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which involved over 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の流行がさらに拡大
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準の複数該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常事態、国際的拡大リスク）に加え、致死率約49%の大規模アウトブレイクであり、承認された治療薬・ワクチンがなく伝播鎖の追跡も困難なため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC国内（イトゥリ州を含む8州）での流行拡大のみが言及されており、Angolaでの発生については記述がないため除外した。Bundibugyoエボラウイルス変異株による史上2番目に大規模な流行で、ワクチン・抗ウイルス薬が未承認である点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de ebola no Congo ultrapassa 12 mil casos e se aproxima de 6 mil mortes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo surpasses 12,000 cases and nears 6,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo reaches 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths since it began in May, spanning eight provinces and centering in Ituri province in the northeast. The epidemic is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain for which no vaccines or approved specific treatments exist. Authorities say transmission remains unchecked due to delays in identifying patients, armed conflict, and overwhelmed health systems. The outbreak is the second-largest and deadliest on record, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa crisis (about 28,600 infections and 11,000 deaths). Africa CDC data from early November indicate only 15% of new cases are linked to known contacts, complicating tracing efforts. Reuters satellite analysis suggests official death tolls may be undercounted in two heavily affected districts."

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、症例数1万2000人を超え死者数は6000人に迫る
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が8州に拡大し症例・死者数が急増、ワクチン・治療法未確立で人道危機・紛争により対応困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（イトゥリ州中心に8州）での大規模流行を主題としており、Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが本文中で言及がないため除外した。Bundibugyoエボラウイルス株は稀少でワクチン・治療法が未確立、武力紛争により追跡困難な点が重大リスク。

article.articleHeadline: Distinct Bat Immune Dynamics May Contribute to Resilience Against Marburg
article.articleSummary: Marburg virus, a filovirus causing severe hemorrhagic fever in humans with case fatality rates ranging from 23% to 88% across outbreaks, persists in its natural reservoir, the Egyptian fruit bat Rousettus aegyptiacus, without overt disease. Bats mount rapid, transient antiviral defenses with tightly restrained inflammatory signaling, whereas human infections trigger hyperinflammation, vascular leakage, and multi‑organ failure. Since 1967, outbreaks have occurred across sub‑Saharan Africa, beginning with laboratory exposures from Uganda-origin monkeys in Germany and Yugoslavia; major events include the Democratic Republic of the Congo (1998–2000: 154 cases, 128 deaths, 83% CFR) and Angola (2004–2005: 374 cases, 329 deaths, 88% CFR), with later reports in Equatorial Guinea, Tanzania, Ethiopia, and Rwanda (2024). In 2007, viral RNA, antibodies, and infectious virus were recovered from wild R. aegyptiacus in Gabon and Uganda, confirming the reservoir. Adult bat infection remains typically 2–5%, surging among juveniles up to 15% when maternal antibodies wane.

triage.headline_ja: マールブルグウイルスへの抵抗性に寄与するコウモリ特有の免疫動態
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はコウモリの免疫学的研究に関する科学記事であり、現在進行中の感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではない。過去の流行事例を背景情報として言及しているのみ。
triage.notes: 記事は研究論文の紹介であり、現在発生中の新規アウトブレイクを報じるものではない。DRCは過去の流行事例として言及されているため参考として記載。

article.articleHeadline: Đắk Lắk ghi nhận trường hợp thứ 4 tử vong do sốt xuất huyết
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dak Lak records the fourth fatal dengue fever case.
article.articleSummary: On 26 November 2026, Dak Lak CDC reported a dengue fever death in Ea Knốp commune, Dak Lak Province—the province's fourth dengue fatality in 2026. The patient, T.P.H. (male, born 2001), developed persistent high fever around 18 November and self-medicated. On 20 November he was admitted to 333 Regional General Hospital; NS1 rapid test was positive, with a diagnosis of dengue shock syndrome on day 3. He was subsequently transferred to the Tây Nguyên Regional General Hospital ICU. At 22:30 on 22 November he was moved to Ho Chi Minh City’s Hospital for Tropical Diseases, where he died en route at 02:00 on 23 November. PCR at the Tây Nguyên Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology confirmed Dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2). Epidemiological surveillance found no dengue cases among the patient’s 17 nearby households in the prior 7 days. Mosquito control: adulticiding at 60 households (209 people protected).

triage.headline_ja: ダクラック省でデング熱による4人目の死亡例を記録
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ダクラック省で季節性デング熱による個別の死亡例（県内4例目）が報告されたが、地域的な大規模アウトブレイクや国際的拡大の兆候はなく、現時点では続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムで毎年季節性に流行する既知の疾患であり、本件は個別の重症・死亡例の報告。周辺世帯での追加感染は確認されておらず、地元当局（CDC）が蚊駆除などの対応を実施済みで、外部支援の必要性は明示されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Tangerang: Jangan abaikan gejala TBC tekan penularan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tangerang City Health Office: Do not ignore tuberculosis symptoms to curb transmission.
article.articleSummary: TB in Tangerang, Indonesia: Tangerang City Health Office urges the public not to ignore tuberculosis symptoms to curb transmission. Dinkes Kota Tangerang head Dini Anggraeni emphasizes that early detection and adherence to treatment are crucial to prevent disease progression and reduce transmission, with family and community support aiding patients to complete therapy. TB elimination is among four health-priority programs targeted for 2027. Nationally, Health Minister Budi Gunadi Sadikin announced a new TB screening program began in 2026. Indonesia aims to provide 10,600 molecular diagnostic tools by 2027 to accelerate case finding and control, up from about 4,000 Near Point of Care devices currently prepared. These devices will be distributed to puskesmas (community health centers) across 7,000 islands to serve 290 million people. The statements were delivered at the Stop TB Partnership Board Meeting 2026 in Bali.

triage.headline_ja: タンゲラン市保健局:結核の症状を無視せず感染拡大を抑制しよう
triage.triage_reason: 結核の通常の公衆衛生啓発・対策強化に関する記事であり、異常な流行や急性の公衆衛生リスクを示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 結核はインドネシアで既知の風土病であり、本記事は啓発活動と国家的なTBスクリーニングプログラム強化の発表に関するもの。新規アウトブレイクや異常事態は報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: New funding for response to Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the DRC, with spillover into Uganda and Kenya, has reached more than 11,700 cases and over 5,700 deaths across eight DRC provinces six months after declaration; no approved vaccine or specific treatment, with surveillance gaps and insecurity hindering containment. Four projects total €15.8 million to bolster the response: an initial €4 million from Global Health EDCTP3 and the EC, plus €11.8 million from Wellcome and the Gates Foundation. EBO-PEP 2026 (€12.8m), led by INRB and ANRS MIE, tests obeldesivir as post-exposure prophylaxis for BDBV contacts. EBONET (€1m) links networks across 23 countries to map surveillance gaps and train staff; EPoCA-BVD (€1m) develops a rugged graphene-based rapid field test; Ebola-Prep TBOX Plus (€1m) delivers practical tools for responders, including a remote molecular test, AI surveillance, a community-health-worker app and an antibody-based treatment.

triage.headline_ja: ブンディブギョ型エボラ出血熱の流行対応に新たな資金提供
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ(ブンディブギョ型)流行は11,700例超、死亡5,700例超に達し、ウガンダ・ケニアへのスピルオーバーも発生。IHR基準複数該当かつ国際的な資金支援が実施されており、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニアへのスピルオーバーが報告されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。承認済みワクチン・特異的治療薬が存在せず、サーベイランスギャップと治安悪化が封じ込めを阻害している点は重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: تفشي إيبولا في شرق الكونغو يتجاوز 12 ألف إصابة ويصبح الأسرع نمواً في التاريخ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 12,000 cases and becomes the fastest-growing outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases, becoming the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. As of 26 November 2026, the DRC Ministry of Health reported 12,021 confirmed infections with about half resulting in death, roughly 6,000 fatalities. The outbreak, declared in May, is driven by a rare Bundibugyo strain with no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. Fighting between the army and the Convention pour la révolution populaire (CRP) rebels near the Iga-Barier mining town, about 25 km north of Bunia in Ituri province, has hampered response, fueling displacement and limiting access to communities and contact tracing. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood or body fluids of the sick or deceased; safe burial is essential. WHO notes access challenges, with about 12 people, including two WHO staff, evacuated to Bunia after three days stranded in Akoui hospital.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部のエボラ出血熱流行、感染者数1万2000人を超え史上最速の拡大を記録
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%・1万2000人超の感染という深刻な公衆衛生インパクトに加え、ワクチン未承認の稀少株、紛争による対応阻害など拡大リスク・管理困難性が高く、複数のIHR/WPRO基準に該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域に『Republic of the Congo』が含まれるが、記事はDRC東部（イトゥリ州ブニア周辺）の流行のみを扱っており、コンゴ共和国（Republic of the Congo）は主題でないため除外した。紛争による医療アクセス制限・ワクチン未承認株（ブンディブギョ株）という点で管理困難性が極めて高い。

article.articleHeadline: У ДР Конго підтвердили понад 12 тисяч випадків Еболи -- Anadolu Agency
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, more than 12,000 Ebola cases have been confirmed — Anadolu Agency
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ebola outbreaks have reached 12,021 confirmed cases since May, with 5,904 related deaths, per the Ministry of Health. The outbreak now spans eight provinces: Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Tshopo, South Ubangi, and North Ubangi. Conflict and community resistance are linked to faster spread. WHO earlier reported that intense fighting near a hospital in Ituri disrupted the response; teams were relocated from Mongbvalu after medical staff were blocked in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours. Separately, WHO and Africa CDC unveiled an updated continental readiness and response plan for Bundibugyo virus, covering November 2026 to May 2027, with an estimated 1.576 billion USD needed to strengthen community engagement, early detection and care, and cross-border coordination to halt transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染者数が12,000人を超えたことが確認された―アナドル通信
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ累計12,021例・死亡5,904例、8州に拡大し致死率も極めて高く、紛争による対応阻害も発生しておりIHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 致死率は約49%と極めて高く、紛争地域での医療対応妨害や対応チームの移動が報告されている。WHO/Africa CDCによる大陸規模の対応計画（約15.76億ドル規模）も発表され、国際的関心・支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Thêm một trường hợp tử vong do sốt xuất huyết ở Đắk Lắk
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Another death from dengue fever in Đắk Lắk.
article.articleSummary: In Đắk Lắk Province, Vietnam, a 25-year-old man from Ea Knốp, Thôn 1, died from dengue fever, marking the fourth dengue death in 2026. He developed high fever on 18 November, tested NS1-positive, and was diagnosed with dengue shock syndrome on day 3; he was overweight and had Down syndrome. He was treated at Regional General Hospital No. 333, then at Tây Nguyên Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology’s ICU, and subsequently transferred to Ho Chi Minh City Hospital of Tropical Diseases, dying at 02:00 on 23 November en route. PCR at the Tây Nguyên Institute confirmed Dengue virus type 2. Epidemiological follow-up of the patient’s family and 17 surrounding households found no dengue cases in the past 7 days. Authorities issued a dengue-control directive: enhanced surveillance, outbreak management, mosquito spraying, and environmental sanitation, with ensured staffing, medicines, beds. Since year start, Đắk Lắk has recorded over 13,700 dengue cases across 534 foci, with 82 foci currently active.

triage.headline_ja: ダクラク省でデング熱によるさらなる死亡例
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムの風土病であるデング熱による死亡例報告だが、同省で年間13,700件超・82カ所の活性フォーカスがあり局地的な感染拡大が継続中であるため、動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムの季節性風土病であり、本記事は既知の大規模発生（13,700例超、82活性フォーカス）における個別死亡例の続報。新規シグナルというより既存アウトブレイクの進捗報告の性質が強い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Congo orientale: oltre 12.000 casi nell'epidemia a crescita più rapida
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Eastern Congo: over 12,000 cases in the fastest-growing outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of November 26, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases (12,021), making it the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic on record. About half of those cases have died. The outbreak, declared in May, is caused by the rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no vaccine or approved treatment exists. Response teams contend with armed conflict, damaged roads, and violence fueled by distrust and misinformation. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood or other bodily fluids of symptomatic or deceased patients; containment hinges on rapid patient isolation, monitoring of exposed contacts, and safe burials. Fighting near Iga-Barrière, about 25 km north of Bunia in Ituri province, has disrupted access to communities and strained treatment centers, with evacuations of personnel to Bunia after days under fire.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部でエボラ出血熱:史上最速で拡大する流行で1万2000人以上の感染例
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、1万2000人超の感染者を伴う史上最速拡大のエボラ流行であり、ワクチン・治療薬が存在せず武力紛争により対応が困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスによる流行で、承認されたワクチン・治療法が存在しない。武力紛争により医療従事者の避難・治療センターの機能停止が発生しており、対応がさらに困難化している。

article.articleHeadline: Los casos de ébola en RDC superan los 12.000 mientras continúan los esfuerzos por contener el brote
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola cases in the DRC exceed 12,000 as efforts to contain the outbreak continue.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 12,000 confirmed infections (12,021) and 5,904 deaths as of Nov 26, 2026. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, declared mid-May in Ituri province in northeast DRC, and has spread to eight of 26 provinces. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for this species. Delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and overloaded health systems have accelerated spread. This is the second-largest and deadliest outbreak on record, surpassed only by the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak that infected over 28,600 and killed more than 11,000. Only about 15% of new cases come from known contacts, per Africa CDC, signaling many transmission chains remain undetected. Reuters satellite-analysis suggests official death toll may be greatly underestimated in two of the most affected zones.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が12,000人を超える、流行抑制の努力は継続中
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ（Bundibugyoエボラウイルス）がDRCで8/26州に拡大し、12,000例超・死者5,900人超に達する史上2番目に大きい流行であり、ワクチン・治療薬が未承認、検出遅延や紛争の影響で感染連鎖が追跡困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナル。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC国内（Ituri州及び拡大先8州）のみが言及されており、Angolaでの発生は確認されないため除外。Reuters衛星分析により実際の死者数は公式統計より過小評価されている可能性が指摘されている点にも留意。

article.articleHeadline: Число заболевших лихорадкой Эбола в ДР Конго превысило 12 тысяч
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of people infected with Ebola fever in the DR Congo exceeded 12,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 12,000 infections, with more than 5,900 deaths. The National Institute of Public Health (INSP) reports 12,021 cases since the outbreak began in April. In the last 24 hours, 66 new infections were recorded, 37 deaths and 25 recoveries. There is no officially licensed vaccine or treatment for the new Bundibugyo strain. Africa CDC Director Jean Kaseya warned that the ongoing spread of Ebola in the DRC threatens neighboring states as transmission continues. The figures underline a sustained, high-mortality outbreak in the region, with cross-border risk highlighted by health authorities today.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴでエボラ出血熱感染者数が1万2000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 12,000人超の感染、5,900人超の死亡という深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、承認されたワクチン・治療法のない新規Bundibugyo株による越境拡大リスクをAfrica CDCが警告しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: Africa CDCが近隣国への拡大リスクを警告しているが、具体的な越境感染の確認国名は記事中に明記されていない。致死率が高く（約49%）、新規Bundibugyo株に対するワクチン・治療法が未承認である点も重大。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak In Eastern Congo Surpasses 12000 Confirmed Cases Amid Ongoing Conflict
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus-driven Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases, with 12,021 reported as of 26 November 2026, and nearly half of cases resulting in death. This is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and the deadliest among Congo’s 17 outbreaks, approaching the 11,000 deaths seen in West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. There is no approved vaccine or treatment. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood or bodily fluids of the sick or deceased. Response efforts are hampered by ongoing fighting between Congo’s army and the CRP rebels (Convention pour la révolution populaire) in Iga-Barrière, about 25 km north of Bunia in Ituri province, driving displacement and hindering isolation, contact tracing, and care. Evacuations occurred after three days of crossfire near Akwe, including two WHO personnel and Congolese health officials.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、紛争継続下で確認症例数が12000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 確認症例12,000人超・致死率約50%という極めて深刻な公衆衛生事象であり、史上最速拡大のエボラ流行かつ紛争により対応が困難化しているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC（Ituri州、Bunia近郊）のみが言及されており、Angolaでの発生は確認できないため除外した。ワクチン・治療薬が未承認であり、武装勢力CRPとの紛争により封じ込め対応（接触者追跡・隔離等）が著しく阻害されている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Több mint 12 000 ebolás eset Kongóban, a történelem leggyorsabban terjedő járványa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 12,000 Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the fastest-spreading outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo faces the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history, caused by Bundibugyo virus with no licensed vaccine or treatment. There are 12,021 laboratory-confirmed cases and roughly half have died, making it the deadliest of Congo’s 17 Ebola outbreaks and likely surpassing West Africa’s 2014–2016 toll of about 11,000. The outbreak centers in eastern Ituri Province, with Bunia a key response hub. Iga-Barrière, a mining town about 25 km north of Bunia, has seen renewed clashes between the army and CRP rebels, hampering containment. The conflict disrupts access to communities, surveillance, and care; around a dozen people, including two WHO staff and Congolese health officials, were evacuated from Akwe hospital after three days under fire. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood or bodily fluids from infected or deceased individuals; rapid isolation, contact tracing, and safe burials are essential.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が12,000例超、史上最速の拡大を見せる流行に
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%・12,000例超のエボラ(Bundibugyo株)流行で、ワクチン・治療薬未承認かつ武力紛争により封じ込めが阻害されており、IHR基準の複数(深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク)に該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーはDRC（イトゥリ州）のみを主題としているため除外した。武力紛争による対応阻害が流行拡大リスクを増大させている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: KDC'de Ebola salgınında doğrulanmış vaka sayısı 12 bin 21'e, ölüm 5 bin 904'e ulaştı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Ebola outbreak in the DRC, the number of confirmed cases reached 12,021, and deaths reached 5,904.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths, per the Ministry of Health. The outbreak, initially confined to a single province in May due to conflict and community resistance, has spread to eight eastern provinces, including Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu. In Ituri, authorities reported 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths before the outbreak was declared on 15 May. The virus is a hemorrhagic fever; the outbreak near the Ebola River gave the disease its name. The Bundibugyo Ebola variant currently has no approved treatment or vaccine.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、確認症例数12,021人、死者5,904人に到達
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がDRC東部8州に拡大し、1万人を超える症例と約6千人の死者を出している大規模流行であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当するため。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株には承認済みの治療薬・ワクチンがなく、紛争と地域社会の抵抗により対応が困難な状況。既に8州に拡大しており、国際支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ost-Kongo: Ebola-Ausbruch überschreitet 12.000 Fälle
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: East Kongo: Ebola outbreak surpasses 12,000 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases (12,021), with about half of patients dying. Declared in May, the outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. Transmission occurs through direct contact with blood or bodily fluids of infected or deceased individuals. Containment is hampered by fighting between the army and the Convention for the Revolutionary People’s Movement (CRP) in Iga-Barrière, 25 km north of Bunia, Ituri province, where Bunia serves as a key response hub. The CRP is among more than 100 armed groups in the region, founded by Thomas Lubanga. Earlier in the week, clashes prevented teams from reaching some communities, surveillance faltered, and treatment centers were understaffed. On Tuesday, about a dozen people, including two WHO staff and Congolese health officials, were evacuated to Bunia from Akwe after three days under crossfire.

triage.headline_ja: 東コンゴ：エボラ出血熱の発生が1万2000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の大規模エボラ(ブンディブギョ型)アウトブレイクで、ワクチン・治療薬が未承認、武力紛争による対応阻害も発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療法が未確立のブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスによる大規模流行で、致死率約50%、武装勢力との衝突によりWHOスタッフを含む対応チームの活動が妨げられている。国際的な支援ニーズが高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: موارد ابتلا به ابولا در کنگو در سریع‌ترین موج شیوع از ۱۲هزار نفر گذشت
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo surpass 12,000 during the fastest wave of the outbreak
article.articleSummary: Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak—the fastest-spreading on record—has surpassed 12,021 confirmed cases, with roughly half of patients dead, making it the deadliest of 17 outbreaks in the DRC and potentially surpassing West Africa's 2014–2016 toll. Initiated in May, the outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no licensed vaccine or treatment exists. Containment requires rapid isolation of patients, contact tracing and monitoring, and safe burials, but response teams face armed conflict, poor roads, and local distrust. Fighting between the national army and the CRP rebels in Ituri Province near Bunia has spurred new displacement and hindered outreach. Transmission is via direct contact with blood or body fluids. The WHO Ebola incident manager notes access restrictions; twelve people, including two WHO staff and Congolese health officials, were evacuated after days under heavy fire related to hospital-based activities in the region as of November 26, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ感染者数、史上最速の流行拡大で1万2000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、ワクチン・治療法未確立のブンディブギョ・エボラウイルスによる史上最速拡大の流行で、武力紛争により対応が阻害されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事本文で主題として言及されていないため除外。武力紛争による対応阻害とWHOスタッフの退避が報告されており、国際的支援の必要性が高い状況。

article.articleHeadline: Faith leaders unite to end tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: At the Union World Conference on Lung Health in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on 19 November, the World Council of Churches (WCC), Stop TB Partnership and Stop TB Brasil hosted Faith, Compassion, and Collective Action: Religious Leaders United to End TB. The dialogue drew religious leaders with decades of TB experience, young advocates, and Indigenous leaders, exploring how faith communities can influence TB responses. They identified stigma, myths, and social determinants—poverty, gender inequality, HIV—as major barriers, and stressed that TB is not solely a medical issue. They urged demystification within congregations, increased awareness among faith leaders and traditional healers, and sustained political commitment. Practical support proposed includes nutritional/food assistance, financial aid for vulnerable families, and transportation to services, with emphasis on continuing support after treatment to address long-term consequences.

triage.headline_ja: 信仰指導者ら、結核根絶に向けて団結
triage.triage_reason: 特定の集団発生や症例急増等の公衆衛生上の異常事態ではなく、結核対策に関する会議・啓発活動の報告であるためシグナルとして識別しない。
triage.notes: 本記事は国際会議における結核対策の啓発・連携に関する報告であり、具体的な発生事例や症例データを含まないため、対象国としてのBrazilは列挙しない。

article.articleHeadline: জাঁকিয়ে শীতের দেখা নেই, পৌষ মাস মশাদের! ডিসেম্বর-জানুয়ারিতেও মশার বংশবৃদ্ধি? সুপার এল নিনোর জেরে বাড়ছে উদ্বেগ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: No sign of biting winter; Poush month brings mosquitoes! Mosquito breeding even in December–January? Concerns rising due to Super El Niño.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, Kolkata and the Gangetic South Bengal region may see extended mosquito breeding into December–January due to warmer-winter conditions linked to Super El Niño. A Center for Climatic Health survey warns dengue and malaria risks could rise as mosquitoes lay eggs and larvae in humid, damp environments even during winter. Temperatures could briefly fall below 15°C for a few days, but most of December–January may stay above that threshold, with humidity and cloudy spells from El Niño-driven low-pressure systems potentially sustaining breeding. The threat is that mosquito populations may persist beyond the usual winter lull into January. Public health guidance emphasizes removing standing water around homes, cleaning containers, using nets, and seeking prompt medical care for fever, headache, or body aches; no exact case counts are provided.

triage.headline_ja: 本格的な冬が来ず、ポウシュ月は蚊だらけ！12月〜1月も蚊が繁殖？スーパーエルニーニョで懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: 具体的な症例数や発生確認はなく将来的なリスク予測の段階だが、気候変動によるデング・マラリアの媒介蚊増殖リスクが指摘されており、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事は実際の感染拡大ではなく、気候条件（暖冬・高湿度）による蚊の繁殖期延長とデング・マラリアリスク上昇の予測・注意喚起が主旨。具体的な症例数・死者数は報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Musim Hujan, Waspadai 3 Tempat Sarang Nyamuk DBD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rainy Season: Beware of Three Dengue-Carrying Mosquito Breeding Grounds.
article.articleSummary: Medan Insight warns that dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes can breed in clean-water containers around the home, not just in buckets or drains, especially during the rainy season in Indonesia. The article emphasizes that even small amounts of standing water can sustain mosquito development if left unchecked, and many potential sites are overlooked during routine cleaning. It highlights three hidden breeding grounds, starting with water-reservoirs behind refrigerators and below water dispensers—areas often forgotten due to their concealed locations. Homeowners are urged to inspect every corner of the house and regularly empty and clean containers that hold water, particularly when rainfall increases, to prevent dengue fever (DBD) outbreaks. Published 26 November 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Cases in DR Congo Surpass 12,000 | SEE News
article.articleSummary: On 2026-11-26, confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have exceeded 12,000, according to government data released today. The country has experienced repeated waves of Ebola outbreaks, prompting authorities to intensify disease surveillance and public health response efforts to contain the virus and prevent further transmission. Ebola is a highly infectious viral disease with severe illness and rapid progression of symptoms, presenting a major public health challenge. Some outbreaks have been associated with high fatality rates, underscoring the need for early detection, ongoing monitoring, and effective healthcare responses to control its spread.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo surpass 12,000, as some health workers have left the area due to violence.
article.articleSummary: Eastern Congo’s Ebola outbreak has surpassed 12,000 cases, with 12,021 confirmed infections and about half of patients dying, as of November 26, 2026. The epicenter is Bunia, the capital of Ituri Province, near the mining town of Iga-Barrière about 25 km north of Bunia, where fighting between the army and the Convention for the Popular Revolution rebels resumed. The conflict is hindering containment efforts, with health teams unable to reach some communities, surveillance of contacts disrupted, and fewer health workers at treatment centers. WHO notes the outbreak as the fastest-spreading Ebola crisis in history, raising concerns about continued transmission amid violence and displacement toward Bunia.

article.articleHeadline: Ação de combate à dengue será realizada na Praça do Centro Cívico
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue Control Action Will Be Carried Out at Civic Center Square
article.articleSummary: On Friday, November 27, 2026, a dengue-control action will be held at Praça do Centro Cívico in Boa Vista, Brazil, from 8:00 to 12:00, in front of the Legislative Assembly of Roraima, with informational materials and guidance on preventing Aedes aegypti. Promoted by the State Health Secretariat (Sesau) in partnership with Boa Vista City Hall, it is part of the National Dengue Control Day. Roraima has recorded 889 probable dengue cases across 15 municipalities in 2026. Eduardo Lira of Sesau emphasized expanding public participation and sustaining vector-control actions, noting that over 70% of Aedes aegypti breeding sites are domestic. A Saturday vector-control mechanical blitz is planned in Boa Vista (8:00–14:00) with Endemic Disease Control Agents. Across the state, activities run through Saturday in Alto Alegre, Pacaraima, Bonfim, Cantá, Caroebe Agroshow (Sat 28), Mucajaí, Normandia, and São João da Baliza, among others.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Bundibugyo: what nurses need to know
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak ongoing in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri province) since May 2026, with 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths across five countries in six months. Most cases in DRC; secondary cases reported in France, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda; outbreaks in France and Uganda controlled by August; Kenya and Nigeria have had no new cases for several weeks and have begun 42-day countdowns to end outbreaks. No licensed vaccines for Bundibugyo launched; Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) may offer some protection against Bundibugyo; three Bundibugyo-targeted vaccines in development; first human trials began in the UK in July 2026. In early November, a British doctor treating Ebola in DRC was evacuated to the Royal Free Hospital, London; recovered and discharged. UK risk assessed as low by UKHSA, while Africa CDC warns global spread is possible via travel; healthcare workers faced violence and misinformation.

article.articleHeadline: ஒருபுறம் போர்... மறுபுறம் எபோலா! காங்கோவில் 12,000-ஐ கடந்த பாதிப்பு!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: On one side war... on the other side Ebola! Over 12,000 cases in Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri province) has reached 12,021 laboratory-confirmed cases, with about half resulting in death. The outbreak center is near Bunia, with the mining town of Iga-Periyar located roughly 25 km north of Bunia, witnessing renewed fighting between the army and rebels that hampers containment and blocks access for responders. Escalating displacement is driving people toward Bunia, the provincial capital and a key hub for Ebola vaccination and outbreak-control efforts. Monitoring of infected individuals and transmission chains remains challenging; treatment centers report reduced staff. WHO Ebola vaccination program manager Dr. Kathryn Smallwood cites security dynamics and ongoing displacement as limiting outbreak response activities.

article.articleHeadline: Kenya : la justice bloque les travaux d'un centre d'isolement contre Ebola soutenu par les États-Unis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya: the courts block the construction of an Ebola isolation center backed by the United States.
article.articleSummary: Kenya's High Court blocked the construction of an Ebola isolation center at Laikipia Air Base near Nanyuki, ruling procedural flaws violated the constitution and suspending work until the terms of the U.S.–Kenya agreement are published and local communities are consulted. The 50-bed facility was designed to quarantine individuals exposed to Ebola, including American nationals, to curb transmission and was part of a US-backed health-cooperation project that faced regional opposition and June protests. Earlier steps included a May provisional suspension and a January contempt ruling against Health Minister Aden Duale for ignoring a prior order. In July, seven American humanitarian workers involved in the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo were quarantined there. Kenya's outbreak nears its end: first imported Bundibugyo strain case in early October from DRC via Uganda; by mid-November two deaths and seven other cases, all recovered; no new cases since Oct 19; a 42-day countdown to declare end begins after the last discharge on Nov 11.

article.articleHeadline: Over 12,000 Ebola cases recorded in Congo's deadliest outbreak
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus reports 12,021 confirmed infections and 5,904 deaths. Declared mid-May in Ituri province (northeastern Congo), it has spread to eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces, including Beni in North Kivu. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for Bundibugy o. Delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and strained health services have accelerated spread. It is the second-largest and deadliest outbreak on record after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (more than 28,600 infections and over 11,000 deaths). The outbreak remains uncontrolled; only 15% of new cases come from contacts known to authorities, indicating many transmission chains are missed. Reuters satellite imagery analysis suggests the official death toll may be underestimated in two hardest-hit areas.

article.articleHeadline: சிக்கன் பிரியர்களே உஷார்! - பறவைக் காய்ச்சல் பீதியால் 3,000 கோழிகள் அதிரடியாக அழிப்பு... நடப்பது என்ன?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chicken farmers, beware! - Bird flu scare triggers rapid die-off of 3,000 chickens... what's happening?
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza (bird flu) fears resurfaced in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, after a Nochikkadu village poultry farm near Kurinjipadi was investigated by veterinary authorities. More than 3,000 chickens on the farm have been culled and buried with a JCB as a precaution. Sanitation teams are disinfecting Nochikkadu and nearby areas to prevent spread. Earlier outbreaks in the district have led to confirmation of avian influenza on over 10 poultry farms, with roughly 50,000 chickens culled. No deaths have yet been reported at the Nochikkadu site, but birds are being sent for examination to determine infection status. Authorities have intensified preventive measures to curb transmission to other flocks and reassure the public.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo: More than 12,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 12,000 confirmed cases (12,021) with about half of patients dying, making it the fastest-spreading and deadliest outbreak in Congo’s history. Declared in May, it is driven by the Bundibugyo Ebola strain, for which there is no approved vaccine or proven treatment. Transmission occurs by direct contact with blood or bodily fluids of sick or deceased individuals; control relies on rapid case finding, isolation, treatment, contact monitoring, and safe burials. The response is hampered by renewed clashes between the army and the CRP rebel group in Ituri’s Bunia region, including the mining town of Igga-Barrier, about 25 km north of Bunia, disrupting access and straining facilities. Dr. Catherine Smolgunt of the WHO notes evacuation of about a dozen people, including two WHO staff, from Akvé to Bunia after three days under fire. The CRP was founded by Thomas Lubanga, ICC-convicted for child-soldier recruitment.

article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak in the eastern region has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases (12,021), with about half of infections resulting in death, making it the deadliest and fastest-growing outbreak in the country. article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en el este de Congo supera los 12.000 casos y es el de crecimiento más rápido
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo surpasses 12,000 cases and is the fastest-growing.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases (12,021 reported), with about half resulting in death (~6,010), making it the fastest-growing and deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and edging past West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic that left about 11,000 dead. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no approved vaccine or treatment exists. Response teams face conflict, damaged roads, and community violence fueled by distrust and misinformation, complicating rapid isolation of patients, exposure-tracking, and safe burials. Transmission occurs through direct contact with blood and bodily fluids of the sick or deceased. The fighting between the army and the CRP rebels in Iga-Barrière, near Bunia in Ituri province, has displaced people and hindered access. Evacuations to Bunia included a dozen people, among them two WHO staff and Congolese health officials, after three days trapped in Akwe hospital amid crossfire.

article.articleHeadline: В ВОЗ призвали усилить профилактику mpox в странах Америки
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO called for strengthening mpox prevention in the Americas.
article.articleSummary: Mpox cases in the Americas are rising, with PAHO calling for strengthened vaccination, epidemiologic and genomic surveillance, and targeted prevention, especially for high-risk groups. From January through November 2026, 13 countries reported 3,269 confirmed mpox cases and four deaths. The United States accounted for 1,457 cases; Brazil 1,325; Chile 143; Canada 108; Mexico 107. In Brazil, a rising trend emerged from epidemiological week 39 (27 Sept–3 Oct), culminating in 246 cases in week 46 (15–21 Nov). The increase was driven largely by Rio de Janeiro state, with modest growth in Ceará, the Federal District, and São Paulo; after two years with no cases, Roraima reported one case in week 46. Mpox is a viral disease transmitted mainly through close human contact, and can spread via contaminated surfaces and contact with infected animals in regions where the virus circulates in wildlife.

triage.headline_ja: WHOが米州諸国にmpox予防強化を呼びかけ

triage.notes: 記事はPAHO（米州保健機構）による米州全体のmpox増加への警告が主題。対象国リストの中ではブラジルのみが具体的な州別データ（リオデジャネイロ州等）を伴い詳述されている。米国・チリ・カナダ・メキシコ・スペイン等は対象国リスト外のため除外。致死率は低く重症度自体は高くないが、拡大傾向と国際的対応要請の観点からPICKUPと判断。

triage.headline_ja: 東コンゴ：エボラ感染者数が1万2千人を超え、史上最速で拡大する流行に
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の大規模エボラ流行（12,000例超、死者約6,000人）が確認され、ワクチン・治療法未承認のブンディブギョ種であること、紛争による対応阻害、国際的拡大リスクも否定できないためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 武力紛争により監視・隔離・安全な埋葬が妨げられており、WHOスタッフが銃撃戦の中で避難を余儀なくされるなど、対応能力に重大な懸念がある。ワクチン・特異的治療法が存在しないブンディブギョ種である点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: En RDC, l'épidémie d'Ebola la plus rapide dépasse 12 000 cas confirmés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the fastest Ebola outbreak has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in eastern DRC has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases, with 12,021 cases reported as of 26 November 2026 and nearly half of those infected dying. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo Ebola virus; no approved vaccine or treatment exists for this strain. It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record and the deadliest among DRC’s 17 outbreaks, approaching Africa’s 2014–2016 toll of about 11,000 deaths. Declared in May, the epidemic is hampered by armed conflict, poor roads, and violence driven by mistrust and misinformation, complicating surveillance and patient care. Transmission is by direct contact with blood or other bodily fluids of sick or deceased individuals. Containment relies on rapid isolation, contact tracing, and safe burials. Fighting resumed near Iga-Barrière, north of Bunia in Ituri, displacing residents and delaying response; about a dozen people, including two WHO staff, were evacuated to Bunia after three days trapped in Akwe hospital.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、過去最速のエボラ出血熱流行が確認症例1万2000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株、承認済みワクチン・治療法なし）の流行が過去最速かつ最も致死的な規模で拡大しており、武力紛争により対応が阻害されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 致死率約50%、承認済みワクチン・治療法がないブンディブギョ株による流行。武力紛争がWHOスタッフを含む医療従事者の避難を招くなど対応を著しく阻害しており、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Восток ДР Конго: вспышка Эболы превысила 12 тысяч случаев на фоне боёв
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Eastern DR Congo: Ebola outbreak surpassed 12,000 cases amid fighting.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 12,000 confirmed cases, reaching 12,021, making it the fastest-spreading and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. Nearly half of confirmed infections have died. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain with no approved vaccine or treatment. Frontline response teams face access barriers due to fighting between the army and rebels of the Convention for the People’s Revolution (CRP), with clashes resuming in Iga-Barriere, a mining town about 25 km north of Bunia in Ituri province, limiting monitoring and patient isolation. Bunia remains a key response hub. WHO notes the conflict has disrupted access to settlements and shortened staff presence at treatment centers. In early week, around a dozen people, including two WHO staff and Congolese health workers, were evacuated after spending three days trapped in the Akwa hospital under crossfire.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ東部:エボラ出血熱の流行が1万2000症例を超え、戦闘の中で拡大
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%・1万2000例超という深刻な公衆衛生インパクトに加え、ワクチン・治療薬のないブンディブギョ株で、紛争により対応・監視が困難になっており、国際的拡大や支援の必要性が高い。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療法未承認のブンディブギョ型エボラウイルスによる、同国史上最速・最も致死率の高い流行。武力紛争によりWHO・保健従事者の避難や対応拠点への制約が生じており、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Cara Mencegah Leptospirosis yang Mudah Menyebar dari Tikus Saat Banjir, Lakukan di Rumah
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How to Prevent Leptospirosis That Spreads Easily from Rats During Floods, Do It at Home
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis poses a health risk in Indonesian communities during the rainy season and floods. Transmission occurs when people contact floodwater, mud, or standing water contaminated by rat urine, entering via skin abrasions or mucous membranes. Risk increases during household cleanup in flooded areas. The Ministry of Health (Kemenkes) guidance recommends simple protective measures: wear gloves and boots when cleaning homes or drains, and wash hands with soap after activities. Maintaining personal hygiene after cleaning flood-affected areas is advised. The article notes several symptoms to watch for, though the excerpt does not list them. Emphasizes at-home preventive steps to reduce leptospira exposure during flooding events.

triage.headline_ja: 洪水時にネズミから広がりやすいレプトスピラ症の予防法、自宅でできる対策
triage.triage_reason: 特定の集団発生や症例数の報告ではなく、雨季・洪水時の一般的な予防啓発記事であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準のいずれにも明確に該当しない。
triage.notes: 具体的な感染者数や発生地域の特定情報はなく、保健省による季節的な予防啓発記事。続報で具体的な症例報告があれば再評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 警惕！呼吸道合胞病毒来袭！这份家长照护指南请收好→
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Beware! Respiratory Syncytial Virus Strikes! Please keep this parent caregiving guide.
article.articleSummary: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infections in infants are the focus of a caregiving guide from Shanghai Longhua Hospital’s pediatrics chief, Dr. Jiang Yonghong, on a Xuhui District health program. The guide outlines a four-stage RSV illness: days 1–3 early with runny nose, nasal congestion, and cough; days 3–5 with worsening cough, breathlessness, wheeze, fever, and poor feeding; days 5–7 recovery as fever declines; 2–4 weeks post-infection cough and phlegm may persist. There is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive. If oxygen is needed, provide oxygen; wheezing managed with inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators; severe cases may require IV steroids. Home care includes elevating the head of the bed 15–30°, saline nasal spray with gentle suction, small frequent feeds, and a quiet environment; avoid indoor smoking and irritants. Maintain 20–24°C and 50–70% humidity; use a humidifier with clean water and no additives; nebulization requires medical evaluation to avoid delays in care.

triage.headline_ja: 警戒！呼吸器合胞体ウイルスが襲来！この保護者向けケアガイドを保存してください→
triage.triage_reason: 通常の季節性RSV感染症に関する一般向け育児・医療啓発記事であり、異常な流行や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: 記事は上海市の病院による季節性RSV感染症に関する保護者向け啓発・ケアガイドであり、アウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Time Series Models Track Monthly Tuberculosis and HIV Coinfection
article.articleSummary: Monthly tuberculosis and HIV coinfection registrations in Sichuan, China (9,012 patients across 132 months from January 2015 to December 2025) were analyzed to forecast short-term volumes with seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA) models. Across 134 specifications, SARIMA(0,1,1)(1,0,1)[12] without drift emerged as optimal by corrected AIC on the full series, though several structures yielded similar information criteria. An independent validation using data through December 2022 identified SARIMA(0,1,1)(1,0,0)[12], which was tested with a 36-month fixed-origin holdout and expanding-window forecasts for 2023–2025 against naive baselines. One-step RMSE reached 17.20 vs 18.74 naive and 25.38 seasonal naive; twelve-month RMSE was 26.30, with MAE worse than seasonal naive. Prediction interval coverage was underwhelming (80% PI 77.8%, 95% PI 88.9%). A five-month holdout for Jan–May 2026 yielded RMSE 12.22 but May counts exceeded estimates, falling below the 80% PI. Annual coinfection registrations declined 10.2% from 2024 to 2025. Surveillance counts reflect reporting dynamics rather than true incidence, limiting transferability.

triage.headline_ja: 時系列モデルによる四川省における月次結核・HIV重複感染登録の追跡
triage.triage_reason: 統計モデリング手法に関する学術研究であり、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威や異常な感染拡大を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は結核・HIV重複感染の登録件数予測に関するSARIMAモデルの手法論文であり、むしろ2024年から2025年にかけて重複感染登録数は10.2%減少したと報告されている。感染症アウトブレイクのシグナルではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Congo, oltre 12mila contagi e 5.904 morti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo: more than 12,000 infections and 5,904 deaths.
article.articleSummary: 12,021 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,904 deaths (case fatality 49.1%) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of November 24, 2026. This outbreak, the seventeenth Ebola episode in DRC since 1976, includes 66 new cases, 37 deaths, and 25 recoveries in the preceding 24 hours. Ituri province accounts for 67.7% of cases, with eight provinces affected overall, indicating wide geographic spread and surveillance challenges. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus (Orthoebolavirus genus); no vaccines or specific therapies are approved, making timely supportive care critical. Ongoing conflict in eastern DRC hampers response and access, with only about 15% of new infections among listed contacts, suggesting transmission chains escape surveillance. The World Health Organization designated this Bundibugyo outbreak as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17, reaffirmed on November 18; not a pandemic.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱、感染者1万2000人超、死者5,904人
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約49%、8州に拡大し、WHOがPHEICを再認定するなど公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクが高い大規模アウトブレイクであるため。
triage.notes: WHOにより2026年5月17日にPHEIC宣言、11月18日に再確認。紛争地域での対応困難により接触者追跡率が低く、サーベイランスの限界が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: 民主剛果逾1萬2000起伊波拉確診病例　疫情仍難遏制
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports more than 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases; outbreak remains hard to contain.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) caused by Bundibugyo strain has surpassed 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths as of 26 November 2026, with eight provinces affected. Initial transmission began in Ituri Province in mid-May, and the outbreak has proven difficult to contain amid ongoing conflict, delayed detection, and an overburdened health system. There are currently no approved antiviral therapies or vaccines for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease. The current outbreak ranks as the second-largest on record by both case and death counts, behind the 2013–2016 West Africa epidemic, which infected over 28,600 people and caused more than 11,000 deaths. The data reflect government reporting from the affected areas, underscoring the persistent challenges in outbreak control within the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 民主コンゴで1万2000件超のエボラ確診症例、疫病は依然として抑制が困難
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）が8州に拡大し12,000例超・死者5,900例超と史上2番目の規模に達しており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク）を複数満たすためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ワクチン・抗ウイルス薬未承認の株であり、紛争・検知遅延・医療体制逼迫により制御困難な状況が継続。史上2番目の規模のアウトブレイクであり、国際的な支援ニーズが高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: La UA celebra el fin de las restricciones de viaje de Catar a Uganda por el brote de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UA Celebrates the End of Travel Restrictions from Qatar to Uganda Due to the Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Africa Union Africa CDCs celebrated Qatar lifting travel restrictions on Uganda tied to the Ebola outbreak and resuming all visa issuances. The decision follows Uganda’s containment of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, linked to an outbreak that originated in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The DRC outbreak began May 15; the Uganda outbreak ended per WHO on Aug 26 after 20 confirmed cases, including 15 imported from DRC, with 2 deaths. The Congo outbreak is noted as the second deadliest globally, recording 12,021 infections and 5,904 deaths per the DRC’s INSP. Uganda’s Foreign Minister Adonia Ayebare thanked Qatar for the gesture. The Africa CDC urged other countries with similar travel limits to reassess measures based on current epidemiology and international health guidance, underscoring benefits to both nations.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ連合、カタールによるウガンダへのエボラ関連渡航制限解除を歓迎
triage.triage_reason: DRC発のエボラ流行は世界で2番目に死亡者数が多い大規模アウトブレイク（感染12,021件、死亡5,904件）であり、国際的拡大・渡航制限の両方が発生しているためIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事自体はカタールによる渡航制限解除に関する内容だが、背景にあるDRC発エボラ流行は致死率・規模ともに深刻であり、ウガンダでの二次感染（既に終息済み）も発生したため国際的拡大基準に該当する。ウガンダ・カタールは対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外。DRC国内での現在の流行状況（継続中か終息かは不明）は記事からは判断できない。

article.articleHeadline: Số ca sốt xuất huyết ở Đà Nẵng tăng gần 2.000 ca chỉ sau 1 tuần
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever cases in Da Nang rise by nearly 2,000 in just one week.
article.articleSummary: Da Nang recorded 2,219 dengue fever cases in the past week, up from 1,925, marking the first week this year above 2,000. Since January 2026, total cases reach 12,555, versus 3,384 in the same period in 2025 (3.7-fold rise). Highest counts are in Ngũ Hành Sơn, An Khê, and Sơn Trà wards. Hospitals are overloaded; Da Nang Women and Children’s Hospital and the Infectious Diseases unit report bed extensions and occasional hallway beds. Health authorities state the rise aligns with the rainy season and variable weather, fostering mosquito breeding; dengue follows a roughly 3–5 year cycle and peaked in 2022. Dengue symptoms include abrupt high fever, headache, myalgia, and retro-orbital pain; warning signs between days 3–7—severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, oliguria, cold extremities—necessitate admission. Three rapid surveillance teams are deployed to augment staffing, beds, IV fluids, medicines, vector control, and patient triage; citizens are urged environmental sanitation and personal protection.

triage.headline_ja: ダナンのデング熱患者数、1週間で2,000人近く増加
triage.triage_reason: 前年同期比3.7倍の急増で病院が満床状態となるなど公衆衛生への影響が顕著であり、WPRO基準（重症度・持続曝露・流行しやすさ）に複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムで毎年流行する既知の疾患だが、2026年の症例数が前年比3.7倍と急増し病院が過負荷状態にあるため、地域内公衆衛生対応の観点から注視が必要。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは現時点で低い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reaches 12,000 cases
article.articleSummary: 12,021 confirmed Ebola cases in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with about 6,000 deaths (nearly half), per the DR Congo ministry of health. The outbreak in Ituri’s Bunia region is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. Fighting between the army and the Convention for the Popular Revolution in Iga-Barrière, a mining town about 15 miles north of Bunia, disrupted containment efforts, displaced residents, and hampered monitoring of exposed individuals. Bunia serves as a major hub for the response, but teams have been unable to reach some communities or maintain staffing at treatment centers. WHO Ebola incident manager Dr Catherine Smallwood attributed the disruption to renewed hostilities, complicating access, surveillance, and delivery of care in the affected areas of eastern DR Congo. As of 2026-11-26, the situation remains unstable with ongoing transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の感染者数が12,000人に到達
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%・12,000例超の大規模エボラ流行であり、紛争により対応が阻害され国際的拡大・支援の必要性が高いため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 史上最速の拡大ペースとされ、武力紛争により封じ込め・サーベイランス・治療提供が阻害されている点が特に懸念される。続報でWHOの正式なリスク評価・国際的対応の進展を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak crosses 12,000 cases as fighting disrupts response
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 12,021 confirmed cases, with nearly half of the infected dying, making it the fastest-growing and deadliest Ebola epidemic in Congo’s history. Declared in May, the outbreak is due to Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Health efforts are hampered by fighting between the Congolese army and the CRP rebels in Iga-Barrière, about 25 km north of Bunia in Ituri province, disrupting case finding, monitoring, and treatment staffing. The conflict has driven civilians toward Bunia and forced health teams to pause in several communities. About a dozen people, including two WHO personnel and Congolese officials, were evacuated from Akwe hospital after three days under crossfire. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood or bodily fluids; containment relies on rapid isolation, exposure monitoring, and safe burials amid ongoing insecurity and mistrust.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、エボラ出血熱感染者数が12,000人を超える中、戦闘が対応を妨げる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で12,000例を超えるエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョウイルス）が確認され、致死率約50%、ワクチン・治療薬が未承認である上、武力紛争により対応が著しく阻害されており、重篤性・異常性・拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療薬未承認のブンディブギョウイルス株によるコンゴ史上最速・最も致死的なアウトブレイクであり、武力紛争による対応阻害が国際的拡大リスクを増大させている。WHO職員の退避も発生しており、国際支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: 南韓爆高致病性禽流感　港暫停進口禽類產品
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: South Korea reports outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza; Hong Kong suspends imports of poultry products.
article.articleSummary: Outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 and H5N9 are reported in South Korea across Jincheon-gun (Chungcheongbuk-do), Yeongam-gun and Jangseong-gun (Jeollanam-do), Gimpo-si and Paju-si (Gyeonggi-do), Gyeongju (Gyeongsangbuk-do), and Ganghwa-gun (Incheon). Findings were reported to the World Organisation for Animal Health. There are no human case counts reported. In response, Hong Kong's Food Safety Centre immediately suspended imports of poultry meat and poultry products, including eggs, from these areas to protect public health. Hong Kong had imported about 80 tonnes of chilled poultry meat and about 11.48 million poultry eggs from South Korea in the first nine months of the year.

triage.headline_ja: 韓国で高病原性鳥インフルエンザが発生、香港が家禽製品の輸入を停止
triage.triage_reason: 韓国における家禽の高病原性鳥インフルエンザ発生であり、ヒト感染例の報告はない。対象国リストに該当する国での発生も確認されず、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 発生国は韓国（対象国リスト外）。香港は輸入停止措置を取った側であり発生国ではないため、ルール6（香港・マカオはChinaに含める）は適用されない。人間感染例の報告なし、動物疾病のみの影響。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak crosses 12,000 cases as fighting disrupts response
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's eastern Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo strain, has reached 12,021 confirmed cases and 5,904 deaths as of 26 November 2026. Declared mid-May in Ituri province, the outbreak has spread to eight of 26 provinces, making it the deadliest since the start of DR Congo outbreaks; there is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo. Ongoing armed clashes between government forces and CRP rebels near Bunia and Iga-Barrière disrupt containment, evacuating personnel and hindering contact tracing and treatment center staffing. Displacements, including in North Kivu, complicate response. WHO notes evacuations after personnel were trapped in Akwe; responders reported gunfire and UN protection. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids or corpses. Only about 15% of new cases link to known contacts, indicating undetected chains. This is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, after 2014–2016 West Africa.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが1万2000例を超える、戦闘が対応を阻害
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が1万2000例・死者5904人に達し、8州へ拡大、承認済みワクチン・治療法がなく、武力紛争により対応が困難化しているため、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: Angolaは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及なしのため除外。既知の進行中大規模アウトブレイクであり、フルRRAでの継続評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Mpox Clades in Africa Show Divergent Severity and Prominent Sexual
article.articleSummary: Mpox clades Ia, Ib, IIa, IIb show distinct severity, transmission, and virulence in Africa, based on 2023–2025 facility data from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Burundi, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. Clade Ib, first identified in South Kivu in 2023, exhibits enhanced human-to-human transmission via intimate/sexual contact and tends to cause localized genital lesions. Clade IIb—driving the global 2022–2023 outbreak through lineage B.1—produced milder prodromal symptoms with low mortality in immunocompetent individuals, with a descendant G.1 lineage emerging in Sierra Leone in early 2025 within household/intimate-contact networks. Cutaneous rash remained the most consistent finding (80–100% across clades); other symptoms varied by clade, host health, and exposure. mpox historically arose as a zoonosis in Central Africa, but sustained human-to-human networks now underpin regional outbreaks. In the DRC, 2023 reported 14,626 suspected cases and 654 deaths; 2024 reported 12,569 suspected cases and 581 fatalities, with mid-2024 WHO and Africa CDC PHEIC declarations. Ten studies (4 cohorts, 6 case reports/series) from Jan 2023–May 2025 showed heterogeneous designs and bias risk.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカにおけるMpox(エムポックス)クレードは重症度が異なり、性的感染が顕著である
triage.triage_reason: DRCを中心に高い死亡率（2023年654人、2024年581人）とクレードIbによる性的接触を介したヒト-ヒト感染拡大が報告されており、WHO/Africa CDCのPHEIC宣言も既往であるため、IHR基準（重大な公衆衛生影響・国際拡大リスク）を満たす。
triage.notes: 本記事は2023〜2025年のDRC・ブルンジ・ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア等の既存データを分析した科学的レビューであり、新規の急性イベント報告ではない。対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみで、シエラレオネ・ケニア・ブルンジ・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアは対象外のため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: COVID-19 VOLTA A AVANÇAR NO ESTADO DE SP; SANTA CASA DE AVARÉ NÃO REGISTRA INTERNAÇÕES PELA DOENÇA | Prensa Mercosur
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 on the Rise Again in the State of São Paulo; Santa Casa de Avaré Does Not Record Hospitalizations Due to the Disease
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is rising in the State of São Paulo, but Santa Casa de Avaré reports no hospitalizations or suspected cases as of November 24, 2026. Fiocruz bulletins show growing Severe Acute Respiratory Illness (SARI) tied to COVID-19 in São Paulo, especially late October to early November, though hospitalizations remain low. As of November 17, 2026, SES-SP records 1,527 COVID-19 hospitalizations, including 485 in intensive care and 206 deaths, versus 2025 totals of 5,169 hospitalizations and 863 deaths at a similar point. Positives rose: Sírio-Libanês with 70 positives in October (19 Sept; 12 Aug) and Santa Catarina Hospital with 98 positives in October (57 Sept; 18 Aug). Fiocruz’s InfoGripe confirms a rise in severe COVID-19 cases. Vaccination remains the main protection; about 90% of ICU COVID-19 patients in 2026 were not up to date. Free vaccination is available for eligible groups; preventive measures advised for symptomatic individuals. In Avaré, vigilance continues despite no hospitalizations.

triage.headline_ja: サンパウロ州でCOVID-19が再び増加傾向；アヴァレ市のサンタ・カーザ病院は入院例を記録せず
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節的な増加であり、2025年同時期と比較して入院・死亡数はむしろ減少しているため、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 既知の病原体（COVID-19）による季節性変動であり、前年同期比で入院・死亡数は減少傾向。ワクチン未接種者がICU患者の大半を占めるという既知のリスク要因が述べられているのみ。

article.articleHeadline: Cercetătorii au eliberat mii de țânțari purtători ai unei bacterii în Brazilia. Infecțiile dengue la copii au scăzut cu 69%
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Researchers released thousands of mosquitoes carrying a bacterium in Brazil. Dengue infections in children have fallen by 69%.
article.articleSummary: In Belo Horizonte, Brazil, researchers released Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in 29 districts as part of the EVITA study, tracking more than 5,000 children aged 6–11; other districts served as controls. Mosquitoes were raised in a former clinic and released from moving vehicles, about 150 insects per container, over several months. Wolbachia reduces transmission potential, and study results show a 69% reduction in dengue infections and 73% in chikungunya; Zika infections declined too but numbers were too small for statistical certainty. The trial occurred during Brazil’s severe 2024 dengue epidemic, when about 10% of Belo Horizonte residents were infected, but treated neighborhoods had far lower risk. A 2021 Indonesia study in Yogyakarta reported a 77% dengue reduction. Brazil plans expansion to dozens of cities by 2027; WHO will evaluate for international recommendation. This is not a vaccine replacement and climate may affect efficacy; Wolbachia can persist long-term.

triage.headline_ja: 研究者らがブラジルで細菌を保有する蚊数千匹を放出。子どものデング熱感染が69%減少
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はウォルバキア感染蚊によるデング熱等の媒介制御研究の成功報告であり、新規アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急性を示すシグナルではない。
triage.notes: 2024年のブラジル・デング熱流行時のウォルバキア媒介蚊介入研究の成果報告。インドネシア（ヨグヤカルタ）の2021年研究は比較参照として言及されているのみで、本記事の主題発生地ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Divinópolis decreta emergência em saúde após casos de sarna humana - Portal MPA
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Divinópolis declares a health emergency after cases of human scabies - Portal MPA.
article.articleSummary: Divinópolis, Brazil, declared a 60-day public health emergency to prevent and control human scabies in municipal schools (public and private) via Decree 17.696/2026. Signed by Mayor Janete Aparecida, the measure is epidemiological and does not constitute calamity or authorize hiring. Provisions: suspend a class when three positive cases occur in a single day; diagnosed students must stay out 48 hours after starting treatment; suspected cases may not attend school or use transport until cleared by health staff. Hygiene must be strengthened in schools and transport after each shift; seating must be assigned to each student during the outbreak. Monitor: two or more confirmed cases with possible link must be reported to Vigilância em Saúde. Families should monitor itching at night and skin lesions, seek care at the Basic Health Unit (UBS), ensure treatment, and inform schools; Tutelar Council may intervene for noncompliance, with support for vulnerable families. Re-scheduling of lessons.

triage.headline_ja: ジヴィノーポリス市、ヒト疥癬症例発生後に健康非常事態を宣言 - Portal MPA
triage.triage_reason: 疥癬は軽症で国際的拡大リスクが低く、既に学校単位での地域的な行政対応（非常事態宣言）がなされており、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威とは言えない。
triage.notes: 疥癬はヒト-ヒト接触で広がるが重症度は低く、学校という限定的な環境での地域的対応で管理可能。国際的な公衆衛生緊急性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Εμπολα: Ξεπέρασαν τις 12.000 τα κρούσματα στο Κονγκό εν μέσω σφοδρών συγκρούσεων
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Cases in Congo surpass 12,000 amid fierce clashes.
article.articleSummary: As of November 26, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports at least 12,021 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,904 deaths, marking the second-largest outbreak in the country’s history. The epidemic, caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain—which has no approved therapies or vaccines—was declared in mid-May in Ituri province (northeast) and has spread to eight of 26 provinces. Violence in the east, including intensified fighting between the Congolese army and the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP), has disrupted response efforts and displaced civilians. Health workers have been forced to abandon affected areas; a hospital in Akbe near Bunia saw staff evacuated after three days trapped by gunfire. WHO incident manager Catherine Smolgun highlighted evacuations of about a dozen people, including two WHO staff and Congolese health workers, to Bunia.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴの感染者数が12,000人を超える、激しい武力衝突の最中
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去2番目の規模のエボラ流行（12,021例、死亡5,904例）が継続し、治療法・ワクチンが未承認の株であることに加え、武力紛争により対応が著しく阻害されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
